title: correlated-load-generator-with-e2e-telemetry-export
author: Daniel Chen
description: Motivation: existing workload runners cover independent request streams (single-sequence throughput, sequence-mix) but do not model correlated cross-stream load spikes that occur in production (e.g., user action fanout, background sync overlapping with foreground traffic). This PR introduces a correlated-load generator harness plus an end-to-end telemetry export pipeline to capture cross-stream latency, queue-growth, and synchronization metrics so that downstream analysis and reporting can reason about tail behavior caused by inter-stream contention. Key deliverables: 1) bench/correlated_runner.py - a new runner that models N interdependent streams with configurable correlation matrices, jitter, and fanout; 2) telemetry/otel_exporter.py - lightweight OTel exporter that emits per-request attributes, cross-stream correlation IDs, and histogram buckets; 3) reporting/cross_stream_reporter.py - post-run aggregator that computes cross_stream_p50/p95/p99, queue_peak_avg, backlog_area (integral of queue length over time), and produces CSV + NDJSON outputs for the existing reporting pipeline; 4) integration test harness (tests/integration/test_correlated_end_to_end.py) that runs the runner against the model stub and asserts telemetry invariants; 5) CI workflow update to run the correlated workload in a short smoke mode on PRs. Design notes: the runner uses event-driven scheduling (asyncio) with a central correlation controller that injects synthetic causality between streams; correlation is parameterized as a matrix of probabilities (float in [0,1]) that governs whether an event in stream A triggers related events in stream B within a time window. Telemetry uses OpenTelemetry traces + custom metric instruments; to avoid high cardinality, correlation IDs are hashed to a bounded dimension and we export representative sample traces at a 1/100 sampling rate in CI mode. Backwards compatibility: the runner is opt-in for the lab (not enabled by default), uses existing bench runner interfaces, and integrates with current reporting consumers. Checklist: [x] add correlated runner and unit tests; [x] add OTel exporter with config; [x] add reporting aggregator and CSV/NDJSON writer; [x] add integration smoke test; [x] update CI workflow; [x] document config knobs (README). Known limitations and future work: higher-fidelity user models (session state), long-running persistence of correlation IDs to simulate multi-minute flows, and a telemetry ingest sidecar for high-throughput on-prem runs. Impact: enables reproducible stress tests for cross-stream tail behavior and provides structured outputs for the dashboarding team to add cross-stream charts.

diff_snippets:
@@ bench/correlated_runner.py +1,8 @@
-class CorrelatedRunner:
-    def __init__(self, config):
-        self.N = config['streams']
+class CorrelatedRunner:
+    def __init__(self, config):
+        self.N = config.get('streams', 4)
+        self.correlation = config.get('correlation_matrix', None)
+        self.seed = config.get('seed', 42)

@@ telemetry/otel_exporter.py +10,6 @@
-def emit(metric):
-    # naive emit
-    pass
+def emit(metric):
+    # attach hashed correlation_id to reduce cardinality
+    metric['corr_id_hashed'] = hash(metric.get('correlation_id', 0)) % 1024
+    tracer.add_event('bench.metric', attributes=metric)
review_conversation: Priya Narang: This looks useful for the tail investigations we've been missing. Two asks: make the sampling deterministic for CI (so snapshots are reproducible) and add an option to throttle exported telemetry to avoid CI timeouts.
Daniel Chen: Added seed parameter (utils/seed_helper.py) and a --ci-fast-sample flag that reduces sampling to 1/100 for PR runs. Updated tests to assert deterministic outputs when seed is fixed.
Ethan Walker: Can the runner blow up memory if correlation fanout is high? Suggest add a hard cap on queued derived events and emit backlog alerts so the reporter can detect overloads.

Daniel Chen: Implemented queue cap (configurable) and backlog_area metric. Added an integration assertion that backlog_area stays below a threshold in smoke mode. Also added a unit test for queue cap behaviour.

Lena Fischer: Minor: prefer snake_case in metric names and include unit labels (ms) for latency histograms. Also asked to include a short example in docs showing how to reproduce a 5-stream correlated spike.
Daniel Chen: Updated metric names to cross_stream_p95_ms, cross_stream_p99_ms, and included example run command in docs/bench/correlated.md.

release_notes: Add correlated workload runner and end-to-end telemetry exporter for cross-stream tail analysis. Includes reporting aggregator and CI smoke tests. This enables reproducible correlated spike tests and CSV/NDJSON outputs for dashboards.
notes: Testing guidance: run `python -m bench.correlated_runner --config examples/correlated_small.yaml --ci-fast-sample` for a quick smoke run.
Backward compatibility: default behavior unchanged for existing runners; correlated runner is opt-in.
Follow-ups: add a Jupyter notebook that visualizes backlog_area over time and integrate with perf-canary dashboards.
